verdict: Avoid for now — Muzaffarpur fruit & vegetable processing scores 44, below the 45 floor; lend only to a proven processor with contracted offtake and a clean working-capital record, and decline first-time capex-led proposals.
title: Muzaffarpur fruit & vegetable processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A fruit and vegetable processor buys seasonal produce at harvest, converts it fast, and sells pulp, frozen or snack product into a buyer's calendar.** Cash leaves the door at peak procurement and comes back months later, so the loan is really financing a stockpile, not a factory. **The value sits in the buyer relationship and the cold chain, not the machine.** Rating work on a gherkin processor makes the point plainly: yield and price move with agro-climatic conditions and hit margins directly [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the crop calendar against the drawing power; if the peak-season stock build is funded by a term loan, ask for it to be restructured as cash credit.

## What has changed now
**Bihar's own tax base is shrinking while India's grows — GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against +6.1% nationally, 6.2 pp slower [D].** That is a demand signal in the borrower's home market, and it is the single strongest reason for the low score. **The peer read is mixed, not broken:** Foods & Inns' Q4 profit fell 16% on lower volumes even as margin improved to 6.6% from 5.8% [4], and realisations fell 25.3% [4]. **Exports are contracting nationally at -9.6% Apr-to-date in USD [D], so an export-led pulp plan carries price risk the borrower cannot control.** Note the peer results are dated June 2026 and the rating material is undated — treat both as directional.

## Where the growth is
**The local pipeline is real but small-ticket: a Rs 3.61 crore namkeen factory at Damodarpur [1], and nine vegetable producer unions including Tirhut receiving Rs 10 lakh each [2].** Tissue-culture plant supply to farmers for high-value fruit is also emerging locally [3]. **Pursue the processor who sells into the union and farmer network on domestic terms, and the snack unit with a local brand and repeat wholesale buyers.** Avoid the pure export pulp converter and any first-time promoter whose plan depends on realisations holding. **Bihar's electricity demand is +14.1% Apr-to-date against India's +9.5% [D] — a genuine tailwind for cold storage and processing capacity, so favour borrowers adding cold chain over borrowers adding plain grinding capacity.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the season, not the year: cash credit sized to peak stock, term loan only for the cold room, and a 25% margin on stock.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly sales register, and quarterly GST returns — the state's -0.1% collection trend [D] means a borrower's own GST filing is your earliest read. **Covenant on drawing power against paid stock, and require the buyer list with credit terms.** If receivables beyond 90 days exceed a fifth of sales, ask for the ageing and the buyer names.

## Early warning signs
**Watch for stock that does not move at the turn of the season, and for the borrower switching from domestic wholesale to export without a confirmed order.** A margin that improves while volumes fall, as at the peer [4], is a warning, not a comfort. **If GST filings show flat or falling turnover for two quarters while the state trend stays negative [D], stop enhancement and review the limit.**
watch: Stock ageing beyond one season -> freeze drawing power and inspect godown
Two quarters flat or falling while Bihar GST stays negative [D] -> stop enhancement, review limit
Receivables over 90 days above a fifth of sales -> ask for buyer names and credit terms
No confirmed order against a shipment plan -> decline the export-linked limit
Cold room downtime in peak season -> treat as stock-loss risk, revalue drawing power
